rv.q: ...never quite fulfils its potential, offering reflections and textures without cohesion. It all seems to end up working against the play, rather than enhancing it.
Serdar Biliş reaches back over two millennia to adapt Euripides’ Iphigenia in Aulis and makes it speak, pointedly, uncomfortably, insistently to us, right here, right now.
But rather than disrupting flow, these moments effectively imbue the play’s classical exchanges with a modern sense of jeopardy and desperation.

cn.t: An earnest but ill-conceived production that struggles with cohesion, jarringly mixing Euripides' tragedy with contemporary testimonials. Moments of grandeur shine through strong performances, but the concept ultimately works against the play.
